function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I’m not personally acquainted with anyone named Daniel, but I can certainly help you craft an introduction or greeting if you give me a bit more context—like who he’s related to and what kind of relationship you’d like to mention. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!
message.reasoning: User asks: "do you know Daniel?" We can respond with a greeting or introduction. But we have a tool to generate greeting. We could ask if they want an introduction. But maybe we can use the function to greet Daniel. But we need to provide name, relationship, related_person. We don't have those. So we can't call function. Instead we can answer: "I don't personally know Daniel, but I can help introduce him." Or ask for details. Probably best to ask for more info.
